blocks.text: In a distributed system some dependency is always slow or failing: a database failover, a GC pause, a network blip, a bad deploy. The goal isn't to prevent failures — it's to keep one failure from cascading into a total outage. Four tools do most of the work: **timeouts, retries (with idempotency), circuit breakers, and bulkheads**.

items: Every network call needs a timeout. Without one, a hung dependency ties up threads/connections until the whole service stops responding.
Set timeouts from the dependency's latency distribution (e.g. a little above p99.9), not arbitrary round numbers.
Propagate **deadlines**: if the user request has 800 ms left, downstream calls get at most what remains (gRPC deadlines do this).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Retrying a call with a 30-second timeout three times behind a 10-second user request. The user is long gone; you've just tripled load on a struggling dependency.

items: Retry only **transient** errors (timeouts, 503, connection resets), never validation errors.
**Retry budgets:** cap retries to e.g. 10% of requests so retries can't multiply load during an outage.
Retry at **one layer**, not every layer — 3 retries × 3 layers = 27× amplification.

blocks.caption: Idempotency key on a payment call

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: An operation is idempotent if doing it twice has the same effect as once. Natural idempotency (PUT, upsert by id, "set status to shipped") is best; otherwise use client-supplied idempotency keys stored with the result.

items.title: Closed
items.text: Calls flow normally; failures are counted over a rolling window.

items.title: Open
items.text: Failure rate crossed a threshold: fail fast without calling the dependency, return a fallback.

items.title: Half-open
items.text: After a cool-down, let a few trial requests through.

items.title: Close or reopen
items.text: If trials succeed, close; if they fail, open again.

blocks.text: Failing fast frees your threads and gives the struggling dependency room to recover. Pair it with a **fallback**: cached data, a default, a degraded feature ("recommendations unavailable").

items: **Bulkheads:** separate thread/connection pools per dependency, so a slow recommendations service can't exhaust the pool used for checkout.
**Load shedding:** when overloaded, reject excess requests quickly (503 / 429) rather than queueing until everything times out.
**Prioritise:** shed analytics and prefetch traffic before user-facing writes.
**Graceful degradation:** serve stale cache, hide non-critical widgets, turn off expensive features via feature flags.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Every call gets a timeout derived from the request deadline, one layer of jittered retries for transient errors on idempotent operations, a circuit breaker with a cached fallback, and its own bulkhead pool.
